UI on BusinessManage > Player Hiring tab (data-testid='tab-hiring'): 3 app-proj-*, 2 emp-proj-*, 2 train-select-*, 2 offer-training-*, 2 sched-change-select-*, 2 propose-schedule-* rendered; sample text matches spec: applicant 'Projected output: ≈ +$9/h − $12/h = net -$3/h (est.)' and employee 'Est. if working now: ≈ +$11/h − $23/h = net -$12/h (est.)'. LIVE wage recompute CONFIRMED: changing offer-wage from 12 → 99 instantly changed app-proj text from '+$9/h − $12/h = net -$3/h' to '+$77/h − $99/h = net -$22/h' (net dropped as expected). Training accept (skill XP credited, owner cash debited by exactly opt.cost) and training decline (owner refunded to within $0.50 of pre-offer cash) both end-to-end green. Schedule propose → player decline keeps schedule, propose → accept switches the preset.

issues: Negative net still rendered as 'net -$22/h' with the minus before the $, which is actually correct — the iter_11 'net $-13' bug appears fixed (sample now shows 'net -$3/h', 'net -$22/h'). Good.

React hydration warning in console: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — caused by instrumentation x-source spans wrapping <option> text in shift/role <select>s. Functional but noisy; non-blocking.

action_items: (LOW) Investigate the hydration warning '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' in BusinessManage's shift-preset/role <select> options — likely a stray child wrapper from devtools instrumentation; harmless but pollutes console.

(INFO) Live ROLE recompute on Dovan's kiosk could not be visually exercised because the kiosk's roster plan currently exposes only the 'cashier' role. Main agent may want to seed at least one additional staffing role on the demo biz (e.g. 'stocker') so that QA can flip offer-role-<appId> and see rev/h change.
critical_code_review_comments: applicant_projection returns 'by_role' map (per role -> productivity factor) and 'output_multiplier' / 'perf' — the FE multiplies these with the wage input to produce the live rev/h figure. This means rev/h is mechanically coupled to wage in the UI (higher wage → higher displayed rev/h), which is a deliberate design choice (treat the offered wage as effort signal), but worth a one-line comment in BusinessManage.jsx calcProj so future devs don't read it as a bug.

server.py:1989 'charge(p, opt[cost])' bypasses bank if cash insufficient because the check at L1987 sums cash+bank but charge() may only debit cash. Verified empirically (owner pre/post diff equalled cost exactly), but worth re-reading to ensure bank fallback works when cash<cost.

server.py:1775 refund path uses add_money(owner, cost) and then writes only 'cash' field — if add_money credits bank first the persisted update may not match the in-memory mutation. The decline test passed within $0.50 tolerance — tighten to exact equality once verified.

Decline path does not include an event-log entry on the owner's side beyond the notification — iter_11 notes mentioned add_event on accept path; decline currently only adds owner notification + player event. Minor symmetry nit.
